test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-acc-001/Biolog.Features.AccessPolicy.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && bash tests/features/bio-acc-001/BIO-ACC-001.test.sh && bash scripts/quality.sh
summary: Round 2 (Chioma's acceptance audit, CHANGES_REQUIRED after both Seyi and Zainab independently PASSed round 1): fixes BIO-ACC-001-QA-01 (High) - GET /api/v1/access-policies and GET /api/v1/access-policies/{policyKey} were deliberately unauthenticated in round 1, reasoning from BIO-IDN-006's own RoleAssignmentEndpoints.ListAsync convention that read endpoints stay open to any asserted actor. That precedent does not transfer to this story: a role ASSIGNMENT list names one person's roles, while an access POLICY's full content - named subjects/profile keys, credential classes, locations, schedules, DENY rules and required assurance levels - is itself the blueprint for bypassing the tenant's own physical security, so an unauthenticated read let any caller who could reach the tenant context enumerate it. Fix: AccessPolicyService.GetAsync/ListAsync now both take the calling AuditActor and require a new ReadPermission ('access_policy.read', distinct from ManagePermission/PublishPermission) via IPermissionGateway; the two HTTP endpoints now resolve the actor and require a verified ADR-0006 Decision 3 provenance proof exactly like every mutating/evaluating endpoint (6 provenanceGate.Require call sites, up from 4). Applies this epic's established 'fix the whole vulnerability class, not just the reported instance' lesson: read is now gated the same way write always was, rather than adding a narrower carve-out.
notes: Verified end-to-end: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj clean (0 errors). 52/52 feature-local tests (6 new: service-level read-permission-required for GET/LIST even for the policy's own author, a positive read-only-permission-holder test proving read succeeds but authoring/publishing still fail, plus HTTP-level missing-actor and missing-provenance rejections for both GET and LIST). 121/121 tests in the full tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests suite (2 real-host tests replacing round 1's now-false 'listing succeeds unauthenticated' test: an unprivileged actor is rejected reading the real shipped endpoint, and a caller without a provenance proof is rejected before authority is ever checked) - one run, no flake. 51/51 offline structural checks (7 new QA-01 checks: ReadPermission exists and is distinct, both service methods take an actor, both endpoint handlers pass the actor through, all four QA-01 tests exist by name). Full scripts/quality.sh (repo-wide gate): QUALITY PASS, 0 failures; contract-freeze PASS (39 artifacts, unchanged - this round touched no frozen contract); secret-scan clean. Scope boundaries unchanged from round 1 (see docs/features/bio-acc-001/README.md 'Deliberately out of scope').
